messages.subject: show x scale/labels for facet_wrap()
parts:
I am using facet_wrap, however the number of plots is a prime number
and hence there is now nrow-ncol combination that will fill up the
plot. E.g:

group <- rep(paste("group", 1:7),100);
value <- rnorm(700)
mydata <- data.frame(group, value)
ggplot(aes(x=value, fill=group), data=mydata) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~group);

Now the problem is that there is no x axis labels for the 2nd and 3rd
column. Is there any way that I can force these axes to be displayed
somehow? Or alternatively, print empty 'dummy plots' for the black
areas?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: show x scale/labels for facet_wrap()
parts:
This may not be ideal, but one approach is to use a 'free_x' scale for
each panel:

facet_wrap(~group, scales = 'free_x')

If you only want scales at the bottom, where 'bottom' could mean
either the last row or the last row with a panel in a given column, I
don't think that's possible at present in ggplot2 per se but perhaps
you could use grid graphics to define the x-scales in those columns
that don't currently have one.

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: show x scale/labels for facet_wrap()
parts: That's not exactly what I was hoping for indeed. I hacked around it like this:

mydata <- data.frame(group, value)

ggplot(aes(x=value, fill=group), data=mydata) + geom_bar() +

facet_wrap(~group, drop=FALSE);


But that is not a very general solution.
